claims.claim: Git folders: per-user branches under /Workspace/Users/, trunk-based strategy, production Git folders updated only by automation, bundles recommended for deployment.
dbutils.secrets.get(scope, key) reads a secret; values are shown as [REDACTED]; redaction does not prevent deliberate transformations.

concept_html:
Production pipeline code lives in Git, not in someone's workspace folder. Databricks Git folders connect a workspace folder to a remote repository, so you can edit, commit, pull and switch branches from the workspace.

The workflow Databricks documents:

  • Each developer clones the repository into their own Git folder under /Workspace/Users/<email>/ and works on their own branch.
  • Use a trunk-based strategy: short-lived feature branches off main, merged through a pull request with review and CI checks.
  • Production Git folders are different. An admin creates them outside user folders. They hold a deployment branch, and only automation updates them, after a pull request merges. Nobody edits code there by hand.
  • For deploying jobs and their configuration together, Databricks recommends Declarative Automation Bundles (lesson A10-L2).

Store notebooks as source files (.py with # Databricks notebook source headers, or .ipynb). Put reusable functions in plain Python modules that notebooks import, so tests can import them too.

Secrets never go into the repository. Not in code, not in config files, not in notebook outputs. Git keeps every version forever, and removing a token in a later commit does not remove it from history. Rotate any secret that was ever committed.

In Databricks, read secrets at run time:

api_key = dbutils.secrets.get(scope="research", key="supplier_api_key")

Databricks redacts secret values read this way, showing [REDACTED] if you print them. Redaction does not stop deliberate transformations, so never try to display a secret. In CI, secrets come from the CI system's secret store as environment variables.

Add a .gitignore for local files (.venv/, __pycache__/, .env), so credentials and environments never get staged by accident.

title: Git folders, one branch per change, and no secrets in the repository
why_html:
A developer tests a supplier API from a notebook with a hardcoded token, then commits the notebook to share the code. A week later they replace the token with a secret lookup in a new commit, believing the problem is fixed. The repository is later mirrored to a partner, and the token is still in the history. The supplier revokes the key after detecting unusual use, and every ingestion job that depends on it fails for two days.

With dbutils.secrets.get from the first line, there is nothing to leak.
